title: EU ministers meet in Brussels over energy prices
text: Energy ministers from the European Union gathered in Brussels on Tuesday to discuss a joint response to rising electricity prices. The German delegation, led by Economy Minister Petra Hoffmann, pushed for a temporary cap on wholesale gas prices, a measure that France has supported since September. Hoffmann told reporters that Berlin would not accept a solution that undermines the single market. The European Commission is expected to present a formal proposal within two weeks.

title: Nairobi hosts climate adaptation summit
text: Delegates from more than forty African nations opened a three-day summit in Nairobi on Monday to coordinate climate adaptation funding. Kenyan President Daniel Otieno said in his opening address that the continent receives less than a tenth of the financing it needs. The African Development Bank pledged an additional two billion dollars for drought resilience projects in the Sahel. Representatives of the United Nations Environment Programme, which is headquartered in the Kenyan capital, will chair the technical sessions.

title: Football: Bayern Munich signs Danish midfielder
text: Bayern Munich announced on Friday the signing of Danish midfielder Jonas Kristensen from Ajax for a reported fee of 35 million euros. The 23-year-old, who made his debut for Denmark in 2022, agreed to a five-year contract at the Bavarian club. Kristensen scored eleven goals in the Eredivisie last season and was named to the league's team of the year. Ajax sporting director Marco de Wit called the transfer a record sale for the Amsterdam side.

title: Earthquake shakes southern Peru
text: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck southern Peru early on Sunday, damaging buildings in the city of Arequipa and cutting power to surrounding villages. The National Emergency Operations Center reported at least fourteen injuries but no deaths. President Lucia Vargas flew to the region and promised emergency funds for reconstruction. The quake was felt as far away as the Bolivian border, and aftershocks continued through the afternoon.

title: Tech giant faces antitrust probe in South Korea
text: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission opened a formal investigation into Nexon Cloud, the country's largest cloud services provider, over allegations that it forced customers into exclusive contracts. The Seoul-based company denied wrongdoing and said it would cooperate fully with regulators. Commission chairwoman Kim Ji-woo said the probe follows complaints from three domestic startups. Shares of Nexon Cloud fell four percent on the Korea Exchange after the announcement.

title: Historic library reopens in Sarajevo
text: The Vijecnica, Sarajevo's historic city hall and national library, hosted an international book fair this weekend, thirty years after it was destroyed during the siege of the city. Bosnian author Amira Hodzic, whose novels chronicle the war years, opened the fair before a crowd of several thousand. The reconstruction, completed in 2014, was financed largely by the European Union and the government of Austria. Organizers said publishers from twenty countries attended.

title: WHO reports progress against malaria in Southeast Asia
text: The World Health Organization said on Thursday that malaria cases in the Greater Mekong region have fallen by three quarters since 2015. The report credits cooperation between Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam, and Thailand on mosquito control and rapid testing. WHO regional director Anand Prasad warned, however, that drug-resistant strains detected along the Thai-Cambodian border could reverse the gains. The Global Fund has committed 400 million dollars to the region for the next three years.

title: Canadian province approves lithium mine
text: The government of Quebec approved plans on Wednesday for a lithium mine near the town of Val-d'Or, a project developed by Northern Metals Corporation of Toronto. Premier Marc Tremblay said the mine would create 600 jobs and supply battery factories being built in Ontario. The Cree Nation, whose traditional territory borders the site, negotiated a revenue-sharing agreement with the company. Environmental groups criticized the decision, citing risks to nearby waterways.

title: Opera festival returns to Verona amid heat wave
text: The annual opera festival opened at the Roman arena in Verona on Saturday with a performance of Aida, despite temperatures that reached 38 degrees Celsius across northern Italy. Soprano Elena Marchetti, singing the title role, described the conditions as the hardest of her career. Festival director Giulio Ferri said ticket sales exceeded 300,000 for the season, a record for the event. Italian authorities issued heat warnings for twelve cities, including Milan and Bologna.

title: Ukraine and Poland sign grain transit deal
text: Ukraine and Poland signed an agreement in Warsaw on Monday to expand grain transit through Polish ports, easing a dispute that had strained relations between the two neighbors. Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Oleh Symonenko said the deal would allow an additional million tonnes of wheat exports per month. Polish farmers, who blockaded border crossings last winter, will receive compensation funded partly by the European Commission. The first shipments under the new arrangement are expected to leave the port of Gdansk in August.
